perspectives.title: Game Remake
perspectives.summary: The game remake feels fresh to play

representative_posts.author: chopchopok.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm extremely impressed at how good the game feels to play. This is a game I thought about a lot during my childhood. I remember the whole story beat for beat, and most of the dungeon rooms as well. And yet the remake feels fresh to play. I keep wanting to play more.

representative_posts.author: hobbit-holiday.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Hey, listen! Love the show, love the game. For me the greatest success of the remake is, for all its differences, capturing the mythical vibe of the original. At what points do you feel this game enhances or detracts from the feel of the original?

representative_posts.author: scoured.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: yeah this is still the best game ever made and I’m glad the remake exists if it exposes more people to it

representative_posts.author: zombieham.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm feeling the same. I liked the original well enough but I wasn't in love with it. But dang seeing people having fun with the remake is making we want to get it too

representative_posts.author: bansheeneat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Ultimately its fine that the game is like this because remakes should be different, it’s just very clear this remake isn’t for me and what I found appealing about the original game

representative_posts.author: dosenozic.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I've lost count of how many times I went through OoT as I kid. Playing the remake now has hit me with all the feelings I had back then.

representative_posts.author: tailiepoe.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The remake for me is bizarre feeling in that it’s clearly been redone in a way to try and make a lot of things more cinematic but paradoxically I feel like the original is way more cinematic feeling even for its limitations of the time??

representative_posts.author: bunnalien.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm still hesitant on getting the remake myself, but... some things I'm seeing are making me clutch at my chest in yearning... it's stirring deep feelings I haven't felt since skyward sword

representative_posts.author: shiversthecat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I hope you get to play it asap bud! If it's that influential of a game for you, I'd love to see what you think of the remake!

representative_posts.author: pudge.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: One worrying trend I'm seeing is a consistent mistrust in the player's ability to figure shit out for themselves. Be it story beats or puzzles, the remake doesn't let you stop a second to notice details and investigate. It grabs you by the scruff and says "Over here! Look at this!!" Key Jingling

representative_posts.author: menutowngames.com
representative_posts.text: man what a good-ass remake, the combat is great... I just finished the second dungeon while taking breaks occasionally and working on my games... now I'm so excited for the adult sections.

representative_posts.author: numbers.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Oh don't mistake me, I don't care to play it because I already own this game. It has zero effect on me, but I don't think more = automatically good game flow. People were glazing Silent Hill 2 remake for having more gameplay but it just seemed so bloated to me.

representative_posts.text: the points brought up here unironically map 1:1 onto the vast majority of video game remakes

Environment.name: Data Center Power

perspectives.title: Data Centers Harm

representative_posts.author: hedylamarr1987.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I want to know how NO ONE really talks about this fact? My girl lives in GA & her town council wants data centers-& all they're worried about is the cost of energy When the data centers will use MORE water than her drought ravaged town is allowed to use! There's 450 folks in that rural community

representative_posts.author: williamac.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The Green Party will never have to honour the commitments they make at the moment. Data centres are the future love em or hate em. Me I hate them, but they need to exist. Unlike the US, UK data centers are closed loop no water supply issues. Just build them next to public pool. Energy is an issue!

representative_posts.author: zachsmind.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I concur we need to find ways to mitigate how "data centers" harm the environment. If I had my way, ALL cars run by petroleum would be taken off the roads and "recycled." Replaced by electric. Every roof should have solar panels. We can't always get what we want.

representative_posts.author: cinematt.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It can’t connect data centres to the grid, it can’t build data centres, they have promised a lot of clients those data centres will exist, and used those contracts to take on an insane amount of debt. It’s not looking great.

representative_posts.author: vambomarbleeye.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: In the US data centres are mainly being built in already water stressed areas, meaning they are draining acquifers and running down local drinking water supplies. All this info is in environmental impact assessment reports from across the developed word. But you won’t know if YOU don’t look

representative_posts.author: niedermeyer.online
representative_posts.text: don't fall for the "it's good because energy requirements" stuff, it also guts tribal sovereignty and gives agencies a blank check end-run around a bunch of environmental and cultural resource compliance law... for mfing data centers

representative_posts.author: sipgoodcoffee.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: In many places it's harder to build more dense housing or a bike lane (two climate goods) next to existing homes than it is to build a data center w/ all its negative climate implications. It's almost as if the purpose of zoning is enforced inconsistently depending on money & power

representative_posts.author: youvotedforthis2.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Build it on some of that arid mountain land to the east. Make them use anti-freeze to cool the system and solar/wind to power it. There is no reason data centers need to be built in the middle of communities.

representative_posts.author: swerto.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A lot of the US's grid is turbo fucked. We have spent decades barely investing in infrastructure. It's just another layer of fucking stupid for all these data centers - we literally cannot handle the additional strain.

representative_posts.author: wowcoolrobot.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: for convenience here is AES' Data Center Terms Of Engagement: No energy rate hikes Energy reliability guarantee Community transparency to approve Local union construction Deliver on job promises Closed loop water system Local infrastructure investments No clean energy or noise loopholes PENALTIES

representative_posts.author: freelancewebdev.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Let's have another look at 2024 while Eamonn was cheering on data centres being built beyond Dublin. This was the year the CSO revealed the existing ones were already using 20% of our electricity, more than all rural households - multiples of any other peer country.

representative_posts.author: cassidyaster.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Locking in fossil fuel production for another generation (which the bill does through project certainty) is bad. Giving the green light to data centers is bad (induced demand will drive up fossil fuel production and utility prices even with transmission reform).

representative_posts.author: larryneufeldsk.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You have got to be kidding: Development banks count data centres as climate finance

representative_posts.author: yvettejr718.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I agree that residents should be informed way before a data center is built in their area. If they are going to be built the residents st the very least should be COMPENSATED for the inconvenience. It’s the least they can do.

representative_posts.author: davisdudepdx.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I wonder if this applies to any other states who struck data center deals? What if we also looked into the increases in electricity and water rates we were forced to absorbed due to deals that were struck?

representative_posts.author: v-ron.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Reporting on data centers being built on military land. Are these plans shielded from state efforts? Not to mention the conflict of interest w/ the companies selected to build them having ties to people in positions of oversight & approval for the contracts

representative_posts.author: autogenragx.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Emporia offers a blueprint, not another corporate compact. Voters approved a ban covering data centers exceeding 10 MW peak electrical load or 100,000 gallons of daily water draw. Replicate the principle: write resource limits into law, not company promises.

representative_posts.author: petersealy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I do have a story from the same school that I’m not quite ready to share yet, but it involved me being unjustly accused of the most bizarre thing (and punished for it). I wish I could say that was the thing that turned me into an evil genius, but the teacher in the next class saw through the lies.

representative_posts.author: johnhudgens.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: She assigned papers on Grapes of Wrath *and* Moby Dick over spring break, by which point the whole class rebelled and refused. She tried to fail us all, and other teachers took over her grading. One of our classmates' mother was on the school board. Said teacher was "retired" over the summer.

representative_posts.author: johnhudgens.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This same teacher declared war on our class, specifically the boys. Since this was an AP class, most of us were in class leadership roles, and she tried to prevent us from attending mandatory meetings that the principal ordered, usually during her class time. This did not go over well.

representative_posts.author: katelambert4.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: ... then she REALLY lost her temper. I've since taught at all levels from kindergarten to graduate school. I often wonder what Circle of Hell that teacher is in today.

representative_posts.author: devonblack.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I was sent to the vice principal's office in third grade for circulating a handwritten petition among my peers, taking issue with a decision by a substitute teacher.
